haiku-low.q1: The indexer deletes the product's search document. Inactive rows are deleted, not skipped, so the product leaves search.
haiku-low.q2: The older change is refused with a 409 version conflict. It is counted as stale, acknowledged, and not treated as an error.
haiku-low.q3: It keeps the partition's offset and retries the failed documents with backoff: 1 s, doubling, capped at 60 s. Nothing is skipped; search serves slightly stale data.
haiku-low.q4: The event goes to catalog.products.dlq with the error text, an alert is raised, and processing continues. The offset moves only after the DLQ write succeeds.
haiku-low.q5: At 20 GB retained WAL an alert fires. At 50 GB ops drop search_slot, the live stream ends, and only a full rebuild restores search.
haiku-low.q6: The alias is swapped in one request, after backfill, catch-up lag under 5 s, a count within 0.5 percent of N, and reconcile, so queries never hit neither index.
haiku-low.q7: Live progress is the Kafka consumer offset, committed per partition as the highest contiguous acknowledged offset, after each write succeeds. Rebuild progress is in the ops database state table.
haiku-low.q8: It resumes from the last committed offset. Replayed writes are harmless because they are versioned, and an equal version is applied again.
haiku-low.q9: A v4 consumer group starts at the recorded topic offsets and replays changes into products_v4 under the same version rules, so later writes win.
haiku-low.q10: Bulk copy documents carry version = S, the WAL position recorded at the snapshot, converted to a 64-bit integer.
haiku-low.q11: The v3 group keeps products_v3 current for 48 h, so the alias can point back in one request. After 48 h the v3 group stops and products_v3 is deleted.
haiku-low.q12: Search is unaffected: the alias stays on products_v3. A backfill crash resumes from its cursor with the same S, and a failed gate leaves the alias unchanged while catch-up continues.

sonnet.q1: The indexer deletes its document (delete request, version = commit_lsn), so it disappears from search.
sonnet.q2: The store refuses it with a 409 version conflict because its version is lower than the stored one. It is counted as stale, acknowledged, and not an error.
sonnet.q3: It keeps the partition's offset and retries only the failed documents with backoff (1 s, doubling, capped at 60 s). Nothing is skipped, and search serves slightly stale data until retries succeed.
sonnet.q4: The event goes to the DLQ topic catalog.products.dlq with the error text and original event, an alert is raised, and processing continues. The offset moves only after the DLQ write succeeds.
sonnet.q5: Ops drop search_slot at 50 GB (an alert fires at 20 GB). The live stream ends. Search is restored only by a full rebuild (C), with a new S.
sonnet.q6: The alias products is switched atomically in one request (remove products_v3, add products_v4). First the gate must pass: v4 group lag under 5 s and products_v4 count within 0.5 percent of N. Reconcile must also run first.
sonnet.q7: Progress is stored as Kafka offsets, committed per partition. NOT STATED where Kafka keeps them. The commit advances to the highest offset where every earlier offset is acknowledged: applied, 409, 404 on delete, or DLQ write succeeded.
sonnet.q8: It resumes from the last committed offset. Replayed writes are harmless because they are versioned: an equal version is applied again and a lower one gets a 409 counted as stale.
sonnet.q9: Group products-indexer-v4 starts at the topic offsets recorded just before S and writes to products_v4 with the same version rules. It replays changes committed during the copy.
sonnet.q10: Version = S, the WAL position recorded at the snapshot.
sonnet.q11: The v3 group (products-indexer-v3) keeps running for 48 h, so products_v3 stays current and the alias can be pointed back to it. After 48 h the v3 group is stopped and products_v3 is deleted, which ends rollback.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected. The alias still points to products_v3. A backfill failure resumes from the cursor in the state table with the same S. If the catch-up gate fails, the alias is unchanged and catch-up continues.
